newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy same-store sales to drop this year.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy same-store sales to drop this year.

text.p: Electronics superstore retailer Best Buy Co. Inc., whose business has slumped due to a recent lack of hot consumer product rollouts, said Thursday it expects sales to drop this year.
Minneapolis-based Best Buy said in a government filing that the crowded sea of retail competition and a dry spell of hit electronic gadgets will pressure sales for the second year in a row.

Nonetheless, the company still expects earnings to increase this year, although it anticipates a loss for the first six months of the year, according to a document filed Wednesday with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"As a result of the higher comparable-store sales decline and seasonally slower volumes, the company anticipates reporting a loss in the first half of the year," Best Buy said. "However, improved earnings are expected for the year as a whole."
For the fiscal year ended March 1, Best Buy earned $1.7 million, or 4 cents a share. That compared with earnings of $48 million, or $1.10 a share, in the prior year.
The retailer's comparable-store sales, or sales at stores open a year, fell 5 percent last year.

Despite sluggish sales, Best Buy intends to focus on higher-margin items such as service contracts and major appliances, which are more profitable than personal computers, for example, the retailer said. It also will offer consumer financing packages and devote more floor space to products with fatter margins.
Digital Satellite Systems were popular last year and helped lift sales, but not enough to make up for weak demand for other video goods, Best Buy said.

The rollout of Digital Versatile Discs, or DVD, this spring and the development of digital TV "represents opportunity to generate new interest in this category in the years ahead," the company's filing said. But the new products are pricey and are expected to have only a modest impact on sales this year.
